PAPERS.title: Urban exposures, frailty, and mental illness in World Trade Center Health Program responders
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM2.5, temperature, Green View Index
PAPERS.n: 18,734 WTC Health Program general responders, later-life residential exposures. A decile increment in the joint PM2.5/temperature/greenness mixture raises frailty index by 0.56% (95% CI 0.14-0.98) and PTSD score by 0.31% (0.07-0.55); effects are larger in responders with higher original WTC exposure, read as acquired biological vulnerability. The estimates are percentage differences on continuous scores, not ratio metrics, so they are small in absolute terms and the mixture decile has no physical unit - a decile shift is not a concentration. Residential assignment at annual resolution cannot separate PM2.5 from the temperature and greenness terms it co-varies with. For distributed sensing the relevant point is that the mixture framing needs co-located PM, thermal and greenness data at a resolution annual products cannot give.

PAPERS.title: Berberine shows potential in mitigating PM2.5-induced breast cancer progression by inducing DNA damage and inhibiting error-prone DNA repair pathways
PAPERS.pm: Water-soluble extract of ambient PM2.5 (Delhi)
PAPERS.n: Water-soluble Delhi PM2.5 applied to MCF7 breast cancer cells increased proliferation, migration and ROS and produced multinucleated giant cells, i.e. genomic instability. Transcriptomic profiling gave a PM2.5 carcinogenic signature enriched in MAPK, ROS, metabolic, lysosomal and ribosomal pathways, with BIRC5, WSB1 and RCC1 dysregulated in patient tumours and reversed by berberine. The inference is weak on two counts: only the water-soluble fraction was used, which discards the insoluble carbonaceous and metal-bound mass that carries much of PM2.5 oxidative potential, and no dose-response or in vivo confirmation is reported. Relevant to sensing only as a reminder that mass concentration is a poor proxy for the bioactive fraction.

PAPERS.title: Grid-based screening of fine particulate matter and water-optical conditions in Southern Benin: the Cotonou, Lake Nokoue, and Porto-Novo Corridor
PAPERS.pm: Satellite-derived annual PM2.5, 1 km grid; Sentinel-2 water optics
PAPERS.n: A 1 km screening framework over 2,589 grid cells in the Cotonou-Lake Nokoue-Porto-Novo corridor, 2001-2022. Mean PM2.5 was 32.17 ug/m3 for 2001-2022 and 32.70 ug/m3 for 2018-2022, roughly six times the WHO annual guideline, with no corridor-wide trend surviving false-discovery-rate correction. Sentinel-2 NDTI tracked field turbidity (Spearman rho 0.488, 95% CI 0.369-0.590) and a red-edge ratio tracked chlorophyll-a (0.432, 0.295-0.544) against 19 stations. Six cells co-flagged at the 80th percentile, but the count swings from 16 at the 75th to zero at the 90th - the threshold, not the data, sets the answer. No ground PM monitor exists in the corridor, so the PM2.5 layer is wholly unvalidated: a concrete argument for low-cost reference-grade co-location in West Africa.

PAPERS.title: Climate-stratified assessment of PM2.5 using machine learning: Geographic controls dominate meteorological factors
PAPERS.pm: MERRA-2 satellite-assimilated monthly PM2.5
PAPERS.n: 49,997 monthly MERRA-2 samples (2019-2023) across five latitude-band climate zones under Leave-One-Climate-Out cross-validation. Tuned LightGBM reaches a global LOCO R2 of 0.367 (MAE 6.43 ug/m3), but zone predictability ranges from R2 0.604 subtropical to 0.142 tropical. SHAP puts 64% of importance on geographic coordinates against 23% on meteorology, and a retrain ablation confirms the coordinates are not mere spatial autocorrelation - dropping lat/lon collapses mean R2 from 0.367 to -0.099. Temporal split validation gives 0.544, so LOCO is the harder test. The honest limitation is that the target is reanalysis PM2.5, not measured PM2.5, so the model is benchmarked against a model; and coordinates proxying emissions means the framework cannot transfer to a region whose emission geography it never saw.

PAPERS.title: Prenatal exposure to wildfire fine particulate matter and fetal growth outcomes in the United States: Findings from the ECHO Cohort
PAPERS.pm: Daily wildfire-specific PM2.5, census-tract resolution
PAPERS.n: 20,034 births (2006-2020) across 30 ECHO sites with daily census-tract wildfire PM2.5 and smoke-day counts. Mean pregnancy wildfire PM2.5 and smoke days were not associated with term birth weight, birth-weight-for-gestational-age z-score or small-for-gestational-age, and distributed-lag and trimester models showed no consistent sensitive window. The single positive signal is large-for-gestational-age, OR 1.015 per smoke day (95% CI 1.001-1.029), which is borderline and biologically unexplained. This is a well-powered null and should be read as one rather than as a failure; the binding limitation is tract-level assignment of a plume-scale exposure, which attenuates any true effect toward the null. Exactly the misclassification that dense low-cost networks exist to reduce.

PAPERS.title: Associations of long-term exposure to ambient air pollution with fracture risk and bone mineral density: A cohort study of 0.5 million Chinese adults
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM2.5, PM10, NO2, warm-season O3 at 1 km
PAPERS.n: 490,172 China Kadoorie Biobank participants, 15,614 incident fractures over a median 12.0 years, with calcaneal quantitative-ultrasound BMD in 32,545. PM2.5 gave HR 1.09 (95% CI 1.05-1.13) per 10 ug/m3 and warm-season O3 1.08 (1.04-1.12); a one-unit pollutant principal-component increment gave 1.08 (1.03-1.13), with PM2.5 contributing 70% by quantile g-computation. BMD fell 0.26-0.31 SD per PC increment and mediated only 5.8-8.6% of the fracture association, so the dominant pathway is not bone density. Exposure is assigned from the recruitment clinic's community, not the residence, and is fixed in space - a large cohort cannot repair ecological exposure assignment, and the 1 km product has no local validation.

PAPERS.title: Unraveling associations between grey-green spatial trade-offs and PM2.5 concentrations using explainable machine learning
PAPERS.pm: Gridded PM2.5 2016-2024; GGSCI, NDVI, nighttime lights
PAPERS.n: Vilnius elderships 2016-2024 under a Grey-Green Space Coordination Index with LISA clustering and XGBoost-SHAP. GGSCI is negatively associated with PM2.5; persistent high-high PM2.5 clusters sit on imbalanced grey-green structures. SHAP flips sign by range: NDVI above ~0.3 contributes negatively in balanced classes, while population density above ~2,000 km-2 and nighttime light above ~18 contribute positively in imbalanced ones. The awkward result, stated but not resolved, is that the most imbalanced GGSCI classes show the lower pollution - which inverts the paper's own framing and points to confounding by peri-urban land use. SHAP attributions are model explanations, not causal effects, and the PM2.5 field is itself modelled at a resolution the index outruns.

PAPERS.title: Field Evaluation of Community Condensation Particle Counters, Optical Particle Counters, and a Low-Cost Particle Sensor
PAPERS.pm: cCPC 0.005-2.5 um number; OPC 0.3-10 um; Sensirion SPS30 mass
PAPERS.n: Three community CPCs, three OPCs and one TSI BlueSky (Sensirion SPS30) co-located at an urban regulatory station for about four months, data recovery above 98%. Against a research-grade reference CPC the cCPCs gave R2 above 0.99 with concentration ratios near unity and a 3% coefficient of variation across the three units - genuinely reference-comparable ultrafine number at community cost. OPC fine and coarse volumes correlated with reference PM2.5 and PM10-2.5 but on different regression slopes, so a single mass factor cannot serve both fractions. The SPS30 tracked PM2.5 and failed on coarse mass, which is the known optical limit restated with numbers. One season at one site, so no drift or humidity-regime generalisation; this is the most directly usable record of the day for network design.

PAPERS.title: Household-specific indoor PM2.5 and PM10-2.5 concentrations and Kawasaki disease onset by age six: the Japan Environment and Children's Study
PAPERS.pm: Household indoor PM2.5 and PM10-2.5, 1-week gravimetric at ages 1.5 and 3.0 y
PAPERS.n: 3,846 mother-child pairs in the JECS sub-cohort with two one-week household PM measurements. Cumulative Kawasaki disease incidence by age six was 15.34 per 1,000. Higher indoor PM10-2.5 was associated with consistently lower odds of Kawasaki disease across exposure categories, with a weaker inverse trend for PM2.5 - an inverse association the authors report without over-reading. Intraclass correlations of 0.52-0.55 between the two measurement occasions mean roughly half the variance in a household's exposure is not captured by these snapshots, and with ~59 expected cases the categorical ORs are thinly powered. Two one-week integrated samples as a six-year exposure surrogate is precisely the gap continuous indoor sensing would close.

PAPERS.title: PM2.5-Bound Metals in a High-Tech Industrial Area of Northern Taiwan: Spatial Distribution, Sources, and Health Risks
PAPERS.pm: 71-site PM2.5 filters, ICP-MS for 30 elements, PMF
PAPERS.n: 71 ambient sites sampled across two campaigns (2019, 2020) in a northern Taiwan high-tech industrial region. Mean PM2.5 was 19.33 +/- 8.97 ug/m3, higher in autumn (23.51) than summer (14.57), with hotspots near industrial parks; total metals averaged 736.85 +/- 751.20 ng/m3, dominated by Zn, Ba, Cu, Pb and Mn. PMF gave fossil-fuel combustion 33.1%, soil and road dust 29.3%, metal industry 22.3% and tyre/brake wear 22.3%. Monte Carlo risk assessment returned a combined lifetime incremental cancer risk of 2.60e-4, driven by As and Cr, and a children's hazard index of 4.65 against 0.69 in adults, mostly via dust ingestion. A preprint, not peer-reviewed; source percentages sum past 100% as printed; two short campaigns cannot support a lifetime risk integral. The usable claim is that PM2.5 mass alone misranks risk where composition varies - the case for composition-aware monitoring.

PAPERS.title: Associations of PM2.5 exposure with diabetes-related mortality for California residents
PAPERS.pm: 1-year rolling mean PM2.5 at geocoded residence
PAPERS.n: 60,824 diabetes-related deaths (ICD-10 E11, primary or contributory) and 119,053 matched controls from California vital records, 2010-2021. Per 2.65 ug/m3 IQR increase in the one-year rolling mean PM2.5, conditional logistic regression gave OR 1.18 (95% CI 1.15-1.22), rising to 1.21 (1.17-1.25) after NO2 adjustment - the association strengthening on co-pollutant adjustment is itself a signal that NO2 is acting as a negative confounder here. The design's weakness is structural: controls are drawn from the same mortality file and are people who had not yet died, so both arms are decedents and the contrast is timing of death, not death versus survival. The $31.2 million per 100,000 avoided-loss figure rests on that design.

PAPERS.title: Replicative and Air Pollution-Induced Senescence: Telomere Dysfunction, Mitochondrial Stress, and Modulatory Effects of Astragaloside IV in Endothelial and Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells
PAPERS.pm: Certified PM10-like urban fine dust, 50 and 100 ug/mL
PAPERS.n: HUVECs and human coronary smooth muscle cells under replicative senescence (passages 6-7, 10-11, 17-20) and fine-dust-induced premature senescence (48 h, 50 and 100 ug/mL certified urban PM10-like reference material), then Astragaloside IV at 50 uM for 24 h. Both cell types showed SA-beta-gal positivity, telomere shortening, p16INK4a/p21Cip1 activation and mitochondrial dysfunction; fine dust drove premature senescence, telomere shortening, TERRA upregulation and acute mitochondrial impairment mainly in endothelial cells, with smooth-muscle cells relatively resistant. AS-IV partially rescued endothelial but not smooth-muscle damage. The dose is the problem: 50-100 ug/mL in culture is orders of magnitude above any inhaled ambient mass dose, so the mechanism is plausible and the magnitude is not transferable.

PAPERS.title: Nasal Exposure to Environmental PM2.5 Drives Testicular Pyroptosis and Tissue Damage: Evidence from Inhibitor Intervention and Multi-Source Data
PAPERS.pm: Intranasal PM2.5, 10 mg/kg, 4 weeks
PAPERS.n: 24 male Sprague-Dawley rats in four arms of six: saline, Caspase-1 inhibitor Z-YVAD-FMK, intranasal PM2.5 10 mg/kg, and both, for four weeks. PM2.5 reduced sperm count and motility and raised abnormality rate, with elevated ASC, Caspase-1 and gasdermin D in testis, all reversed by the inhibitor - a coherent NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptosis chain. Reanalysis of GEO GSE189187 (GC-2spd cells, 3 vs 3) gave 217 DEGs enriched in interferon/antiviral processes, with Hmox1 up and Stat1 down. n=6 per arm and a 3-vs-3 public dataset cannot support hub-gene claims, and intranasal instillation at 10 mg/kg bears no quantitative relation to ambient inhalation. Preprint, no peer review.

PAPERS.title: Integrating GPS and Low-Cost Sensors to Enhance Personal PM2.5 Exposure Modeling for Schoolchildren
PAPERS.pm: Portable PM2.5 sensor with GPS, 918 person-days; BAM-1020 reference
PAPERS.n: 918 person-days from northern Taiwan schoolchildren over one year with GPS-equipped portable PM2.5 sensors, pre-deployment calibrated against a Met One BAM-1020 (mean R2 0.996, slope 0.962). Personal exposure was dominated by within-subject variability (ICC 0.125); school was the highest-concentration microenvironment at 22.7 ug/m3. The fully GPS-resolved microenvironment model reached R2 0.619 (74.0% accuracy) and a home-plus-school-only model 0.616 (71.7%) - so essentially all the gain comes from identifying two microenvironments, and full trajectory resolution adds nothing. That negative result is the useful one for network design: it sets a ceiling on what finer location data buys. Validation is internal against concurrent personal measurement; whether the models reduce exposure misclassification in health analysis is explicitly not tested.

PAPERS.title: Leveraging multi-source observations for vertical PM2.5 estimation: A deep learning fusion model
PAPERS.pm: Lidar extinction, microwave radiometer profiles, tower PM2.5 at 200/300 m
PAPERS.n: An AM-CNN-BiLSTM fusion model estimating PM2.5 at 200 and 300 m on the Shenzhen Meteorological Gradient Tower, July 2022-June 2023, combining lidar aerosol extinction coefficient, microwave-radiometer thermodynamic profiles, meteorology and tower PM2.5. Chronological test split with an expanding window gave R2 0.87 at 200 m and 0.83 at 300 m, beating baselines; SHAP, ablation and sensitivity analysis all identify extinction coefficient as the dominant constraint, with RH, temperature and wind complementary. The authors state plainly that the learned extinction-PM2.5 and humidity relations are site-specific and need multi-year cross-site validation - with one tower and one year that caveat is binding. Still the cleanest demonstration that lidar plus profiler can substitute for vertical in-situ nodes.

PAPERS.title: Turbulence-Induced Size Redistribution of Submicron NaCl Aerosols in Ribbed Confined Flows Prior to Electrostatic Collection
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only (no abstract deposited)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only. Crossref deposited this DOI on 12 September with no abstract, and per-DOI retries against Crossref, Europe PMC and PubMed all returned nothing - the expected same-day Elsevier deposit gap. Carried on title alone because submicron size redistribution in confined turbulent flow directly governs what reaches an inlet, and no finding is asserted here. On the retry list for a later issue.

PAPERS.title: Coupled Effects of Core Material and Aggregate Morphology on the Optical Properties of Atmospheric Aerosols
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only (no abstract deposited)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref, Europe PMC or PubMed on per-DOI retry. Retained on title because core composition and aggregate morphology set the scattering cross-section that every optical PM sensor inverts to mass, which is the physical root of the humidity and composition dependence seen in co-location studies. No finding is asserted. On the retry list.

PAPERS.title: Long-term CALIOP observations of vertical aerosol stratification over Shanghai: Meteorological modulation and height-resolved transport
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only (no abstract deposited); CALIOP spaceborne lidar
PAPERS.n: Metadata only - no abstract deposited to Crossref and none in Europe PMC or PubMed on per-DOI retry. Carried on title because height-resolved spaceborne lidar climatology over a megacity is the long-record complement to the single-tower fusion result in this same issue, and because column-to-surface conversion error is the central obstacle for satellite PM2.5. No finding asserted. On the retry list.

PAPERS.title: Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) analysis and 16S rRNA gene sequencing of indoor air pollutants in a 3000-capacity religious auditorium
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only (no abstract deposited)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; abstract absent from Crossref, Europe PMC and PubMed on per-DOI retry. Retained because a 3,000-capacity assembly space is a high-occupancy indoor microenvironment where occupant-generated coarse particles and bioaerosol dominate, and 16S sequencing of airborne material is particulate characterisation. PM scope is inferred from the title, no finding asserted, and the study location is not recoverable from metadata. On the retry list.

PAPERS.title: Association of Environmental Factors and Aging Levels Under Different Urbanization Levels in China
PAPERS.pm: County-level annual PM2.5, CO, SO2, O3; 2010 and 2020
PAPERS.n: County-level Chinese data for 2010 and 2020, 22 candidate factors, fixed-effect and random-forest models against the 65+ and 85+ population shares, stratified by high, medium and low urbanisation. Ageing levels rose 1.5-2.1 fold over the decade. PM2.5 and resident savings rank among the important variables in low-urbanisation counties; in medium-urbanisation counties CO, SO2, PM2.5 and O3 all enter; in high-urbanisation counties January and July mean temperature dominate instead. The design cannot support a health claim: ageing share is a demographic composition driven chiefly by migration and fertility, and variable-importance rankings from random forests on two cross-sections are not effect estimates. Carried for the policy-facing exposure gradient, not for causation.

PAPERS.title: Breathing carcinogens: PM2.5 air pollution and lung cancer in never-smokers, a narrative review
PAPERS.pm: Narrative synthesis, PM2.5 exposure literature 2000-May 2026
PAPERS.n: Narrative review of PM2.5 and lung cancer in never-smokers, PubMed/MEDLINE 2000 to May 2026 plus reference-list snowballing. The central claim is mechanistic rather than quantitative: PM2.5 acts predominantly as a tumour promoter rather than a direct mutagen, operating through inflammatory signalling, metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic change, and is associated with more advanced stage at diagnosis and worse survival after resection. Lung cancer in never-smokers is described as molecularly and immunologically distinct, with screening and precision-oncology implications. No pooled estimate, no risk-of-bias assessment and no search-yield count are reported, so it carries no quantitative weight and the selection is author-curated by design. Useful as a mechanism map, not as evidence.
